questions.prompt: What does 'API' stand for?
questions.did_you_know: APIs let software components communicate — your favorite apps use hundreds of them.

questions.prompt: Which data structure processes elements in First-In, First-Out (FIFO) order?
questions.did_you_know: Queues power everything from print spoolers to real-time message brokers.

questions.prompt: What does 'HTTP' stand for?
questions.did_you_know: HTTP was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989 to share documents across the web.

questions.prompt: Which sorting algorithm has an average-case time complexity of O(n log n)?
questions.did_you_know: Merge Sort was invented by John von Neumann in 1945 and is still widely used today.

questions.prompt: What is a 'version control system' primarily used for?
questions.did_you_know: Git, the most popular VCS, was created by Linus Torvalds in just two weeks in 2005.

questions.prompt: What term describes content that spreads rapidly and widely online?
questions.did_you_know: The word 'viral' in the internet sense dates back to the late 1990s.

questions.prompt: What decade is widely regarded as the golden age of arcade video games?
questions.did_you_know: Pac-Man, Donkey Kong, and Space Invaders all launched in the early 1980s.

questions.prompt: In internet culture, what is a 'meme'?
options: A shareable idea, image, or joke that spreads online
questions.did_you_know: Richard Dawkins coined 'meme' in 1976 — long before the internet gave it new life.

questions.prompt: What music format succeeded the CD as the dominant way people listen to music?
questions.did_you_know: By 2015, music streaming surpassed album sales for the first time in the US.

questions.prompt: What does 'cosplay' refer to?
options: Dressing up as a fictional character
questions.did_you_know: The word 'cosplay' was coined in 1984 by a journalist after attending a US fan convention.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.did_you_know: Au comes from the Latin 'aurum' — gold has been prized by humans for over 6,000 years.

questions.prompt: What force keeps planets in orbit around the sun?
questions.did_you_know: Newton formulated the law of gravity after observing a falling apple — or so the popular story goes.

questions.prompt: Which organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.did_you_know: Mitochondria have their own DNA, supporting the theory that they were once free-living bacteria.

questions.prompt: What is the approximate speed of light in a vacuum?
questions.did_you_know: Nothing with mass can reach light speed — doing so would require infinite energy.

questions.prompt: Which subatomic particle carries a negative electric charge?
questions.did_you_know: Electrons were discovered by J.J. Thomson in 1897 — the first subatomic particle ever identified.

questions.prompt: In what year did the first crewed moon landing occur?
questions.did_you_know: Apollo 11 landed on July 20, 1969. Neil Armstrong's first steps were broadcast to 600 million viewers.

questions.prompt: Which of the Seven Ancient Wonders is still standing today?
questions.did_you_know: The Great Pyramid at Giza is the only Ancient Wonder that has survived to the present day.

questions.prompt: What invention is Johannes Gutenberg famous for (around 1440)?
questions.did_you_know: Gutenberg's press made books affordable, accelerating the spread of knowledge across Europe.

questions.prompt: Julius Caesar was the leader of which empire?
questions.did_you_know: Caesar was assassinated in 44 BC, yet his name lives on — 'Kaiser' and 'Czar' both derive from it.

questions.prompt: What was the name of the first artificial satellite launched into Earth orbit?
questions.did_you_know: Sputnik 1 was launched by the Soviet Union on October 4, 1957, marking the start of the Space Age.

questions.prompt: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.did_you_know: The Mona Lisa draws about 20,000 visitors per day at the Louvre — it's the world's most visited painting.

questions.prompt: What is the art of creating images from small pieces of colored glass or stone called?
questions.did_you_know: Roman mosaics created 2,000 years ago are so durable that many are still preserved today.

questions.prompt: Which art movement is most associated with Salvador Dalí?
questions.did_you_know: Surrealism drew on Freudian ideas to explore the unconscious mind through dreamlike imagery.

questions.prompt: What tool does an orchestra conductor typically use to direct the ensemble?
questions.did_you_know: The conductor's baton became standard in the 19th century, replacing earlier tools like rolled-up paper.

questions.prompt: What does 'a cappella' mean in music?
questions.did_you_know: A cappella means 'in the chapel style' in Italian — early church music was often unaccompanied.

questions.prompt: How many players does each team field on a basketball court at one time?
questions.did_you_know: Basketball was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891 using a peach basket as the original goal.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum score possible in a single frame of ten-pin bowling?
questions.did_you_know: A perfect 'turkey' (three strikes) can score 30 in one frame; 12 straight strikes = a perfect game of 300.

questions.prompt: In soccer, what does it mean to score an 'own goal'?
options: Score the ball into your own net
questions.did_you_know: Own goals are surprisingly common — roughly 1 in 20 goals scored in top leagues are accidental own goals.

questions.prompt: How long is a standard marathon race?
questions.did_you_know: The marathon distance was standardized at the 1908 London Olympics to suit the royal family's viewing position.

questions.prompt: Which sport uses the scoring terms 'love', 'deuce', and 'advantage'?
questions.did_you_know: In tennis, 'love' means zero — possibly from the French 'l'œuf' (egg), which resembles the number 0.
